fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. The value is the color words separated by single spaces, with no brackets, quotes or commas; at step #1 it is the word none. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. That held-then-released event is always one completed bin placement: count it regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. Example sequence over an episode: none -> none -> green -> green -> green green. e.g. blue blue blue green

fields.name: arrivals
fields.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes currently lying on the table, in the order they first appeared in the episode, oldest first. Goal-color cubes are not all present at the start: new ones appear on the table while the robot works, and the oracle picks, within the color being worked, the one that has been on the table longest. At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene (a cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed). With one goal-color cube in the scene the list is that cube. With several, the scene gives no arrival order, so the annotator, reading the whole episode, lists first the pre-existing cubes the oracle actually picks during the episode in the order it picks them (first-picked first), and after them the never-picked cubes of a needed color ordered by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first (two within about 3 px of the same distance: larger x first), skipping detections within about 28 px of that center. At each later step, in order: (1) removal, only at a pick-up step (one whose execution frames show the fingers going from open to about 46% while the gripper is over a table cube, followed by a held line): remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in that closing frame. At a put-into-bin step, where the first execution frame already shows a cube held, remove nothing (the held cube's entry was already removed at its pick-up step). Never remove an entry that still has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; the 12 px test is never stretched to the nearest entry. (2) retention: matching is one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new. An entry with a match is kept and refreshed to that position; the bin-echo and release-echo exclusions do not apply here, so an entry matching a detection near the just-released cube's last reported position or near the gripper at release is kept. An entry with no such detection is dropped. (3) appending: every goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended, except bin echoes and release echoes. A bin echo is a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was present in the scene at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step; a detection of a color not yet in `placed` that first appears during the step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the scene at the decision step is a genuine new cube however near the bin it lies, and is appended in order of first appearance. The release frame is the first execution frame in which the fingers are about 100% open and no object line says held (a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it). A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appears in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moves a few px along with the retreating gripper over the following frames; it is never appended however far it is from the bin center. A detection is not an echo if it matches an existing entry within about 12 px or was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. A goal-color detection that appears during the step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and then stays put is a genuine new arrival and is appended. In a pick-up step (one that ends with a cube held and has no release frame) there is no release echo and no moved-with-the-gripper exclusion: every new goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that is not a bin echo is appended, even one within a dozen px of the gripper or of the just-grasped cube. (4) when several detections are appended in one step, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared (earliest first), tracking each across frames within about 12 px; two that first appear in the same frame follow that frame's listing order. Example over a step in which a green cube appeared at [86, 143] in an early frame and another at [86, 95] in a later frame, with [86, 119] picked up: [[86, 143], [86, 95]]. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
